newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: DOWNER WELCOMES HEBRON AGREEMENT
Foreign Minister, Alexander Downer, has welcomed the Hebron agreement.
Mr Downer says he hopes the agreeement will defuse the tension and prevent any further violence and loss of life.
He's called for progress on the remaining aspects of the interim agreement and urged all sides to avoid actions which would lead to renewed tensions.
AMA WILL BACK MOVES TO BOOST IMMUNISATION
The Australian Medical Association says it will support any sensible measure to improve Australian immunisation rates.
The AMA says its pleased to see Dr Wooldridge's commitment to increasing immunisation rates.
It suggests Dr Wooldridge should declare an annual immunisation week to promote vaccination.
The AMA says parents should check their children's immunisation is up to date while preparing to go back to school in the next few weeks.
EUTHANASIA CAMPAIGNER IDENTIFIES THOSE WHO WANT TO DIE
Voluntary euthanasia campaigner Dr Phillip Nitschke says women and people from poorer backgrounds feature prominently among those seeking to use the Northern Territory's Right To Die law.
In his submission to the Senate Committee examining the law, Dr Nitschke claims about 40 people wanting assisted suicides have approached him, since the law was passed.
He says these people predominately come from the over-60, female, and lower socio-economic categories of cancer sufferers. - - - -
DEMOCRATS LABEL REVIEW AS POST MORTEM
The Australian Democrats says it can't see the Federal Government's logic in commissioning a review into higher education, after implementing radical and devastating reforms to the system.
The Government has outlined details of an independent panel committee to supervise planned changes to Australia's higher education system.
Democrats spokesman on higher education, Natasha Stott-Despoja says the committee will be performing a post mortem...rather than a review...of higher education.
Meanwhile Federal Education Minister Amanda Vanstone denies students and teaching staff have been excluded from the review process....after claims they've been left off the panel.
CALL FOR TAX BREAKS FOR HIGH ROLLER GAMBLERS
The Tourism Council of Australia says Australia will miss out on tours of high roller gamblers to its casinos, unless tax breaks are offered.
That follows billionaire Kerry Packer's call for a tax break for high roller gamblers at the Sydney Harbour Casino, to 10 per cent, in line with Queensland and Victoria.
Tourism Council Managing director, Bruce Baird, says if high rollers aren't given a tax reprieve in New South Wales, they'll avoid Australia and operate in other countries.
INDUSTRIAL ACTION AT BHP SITE CONTINUES
Workers at BHP's one-point-five billion dollar hot briquetted iron plant in West Australia say they won't return to work because they don't trust the project's contractors.
More than 600 workers walked off the job at the Port Hedland site earlier this month seeking wages up to 38-per cent above award rates and a living away from home allowance of 500 dollars a week.
The Industrial Relations Commission recommended they return to work, but a meeting of workers this morning rejected the proposal.
Manufacturing Union Organiser, Colin Saunders, says workers believe the contractors have had 12 months to fix wage conditions and are simply stalling.
UPDATE OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN
Australia's Annabel Ellwood has bowed-out of the Australian Open, going down to Germany's Marketa Kochta.
Kochta won 6-love, 4-6, 6-1.
Earlier, Todd Woodbridge advanced to the third round, with a straight-sets win over Frenchman, Stephane Simian.
Another Australian, Richard Fromberg also has a chance to advance, when he plays seventh seed, Thomas Enqvist, on centre court shortly.
Meanwhile, women's top seed, Steffi Graf, has beaten Latvia's Larisa Neiland, 7-5, 6-2.
Others through today include former women's champion, Mary Pierce, and men's second seed, Michael Chang.
WALLABY JUMPER CHANGED
The Australian Rugby Union has changed the traditional all-gold Wallaby jumper.
Chief Executive of the ARU, John O'Neill, has admitted he felt some reluctance to change the jumper.
Mr O'Neill says the new design strikes a balance between tradition and commercial reality, and is in response to the ARU's new multi-million dollar sponsor and its merchandising plans.
He says pre-sales of the new outfit show sports retailers have endorsed the change.
